questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Staying in the EU but at a good university where i had travel options.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go go go

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Unibo has a great site for general information. Google 'unibo onlime mobility' and you can find a lot. 
Finding faculty specific information was difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You have to check-in online and then you get some useful emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I believe there was a video orientation meeting that i did not attend. I would recommend it if you have a faculty specific one, otherwise the information is mostly the website.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I Used DoveVivo which was an expensive solution because of high fees, but they are legit. 
I heard of multiple people who got scammed through whatsapp. 

I think unibo links to portals where you can find housing. I did not use it

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to find, so you have to start looking early - like really early

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is expensive and difficult to find.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
You get the info in the mail after your check-in

As for learning agreement it is more difficult.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
At Unibo you register for exams, not courses. 
You register for the exams a few week before they take place.
In order to register for the exam you have to put the courses in the study plan. 

Only those courses in the course catalog that have a published time table are available for registration. Unibo post these time tables rather late, so it can be difficult to start early. 

For the Learning Agreement there are different rules according to faculty that dictate which courses you are allowed to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact your faculties incoming student desk via email. In my experience they were slow in supply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a difficult process but in the end we found a solution so i could take the courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Contact your specific faculty ahead of time and ask if there are specific rules for that faculty. 
For example bachelor/undergraduate econ student are not allowed to take master/graduate courses - this rule does not apply to other faculties, that i know of.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Unibo has many courses to chose from.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
In general the level is lower than at UCPH, but can vary from course to course. 
It is easier to get a high grade than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
They use slides like we are use to. 
In none of my courses did we have assigment during the duration of the course. 
But i know that in many courses student must do a presentation during the course as part of the final grade. 
The information on grading and exam style can be found in the course catalog. 

Some courses last from september to december with exam either in december or january
Some courses last from september to october with exam in october 
Some courses last from november to december with exam in december/january

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intro to python for economists (6 ECTS, graduate course)
International finance (6 ECTS, graduate course)
International Economics (6 ECTS, graduate course)
Health economics and policies in low and middel income countries (6 ECTS, graduate course)
Public economics (8 ECTS, undergraduate course)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All, they were very good. 

But not graduate courses if you are an econ bachelor student. You are not allowed to take graduate courses. I was allowed because i was so late in making my learning agreement.

questions.answer:
drinks were less expensive than in Denmark. 
Groceries were not as inexpensive as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not know of any activities provided by unibo.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of people used ESN Bologna, who organized a lot of fun things for exchange students. Follow them on instagram.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Travel. Bologna is perfectly placed to visit a lot of the great italian cities. 
Modena, Parma, Ravenna, Ferrara, Siena, Verona, Venice, Rome, Rimini

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the sites.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get a drink at Piazza Verdi - there are always a lot of students. And the italians are super friendly

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Not all italians speak english. 
They can be very stubborn

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness and generosity

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the city - don't worry too much about school. 

Walk around a lot and get to know every street

take it easy - everything works out in the end

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Learn a little italian - it is fun and the people will be more sympathetic towards you if you show interest and try.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends i got and the way that Bologna feels like home now.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my learning agreement

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
